Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. - a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. ## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f7cb52d1524b80e77b672c81fbb5d6f8add100b3`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/hono-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/cors-default-admission.test.ts, packages/qa/http-conformance/src/hono-approvals-act.conformance.test.ts, packages/qa/http-conformance/src/hono-webhooks-redeliver.conformance.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-metrics-inbound-coverage.hono.integration.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/pattern-matcher.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/package.json, packages/core/src/stack-auth.ts, packages/core/src/index.ts, packages/core/src/kernel.ts, packages/core/src/kernel-base.ts, packages/core/src/lite-kernel.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-dev/src/dev-plugin.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts, packages/types/src/env.ts, packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts, content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx, content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, .changeset/config.json, .changeset/pre.json, .changeset/24341-extend-default-row-scope-refused.md; the six prose faces (.changeset/24738-cors-default-no-cross-origin-caller.md, docs/HARDENING.md, content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx, content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx, content/docs/deployment/production-readiness.mdx, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/README.md) read sentence by sentence against the code.

Net diff read as merge-base `46bb5e3e5` to the head (12 files, +391/-50). `main` has moved one commit past that merge-base and touches none of the paths above.

### ① Derived judgments

**Disclosure (security card, ruling on #9387, comment 5323310017).**
- The PR's artifacts are its title, body, the changeset, the five doc faces, the code comments in `hono-plugin.ts` and `adapter.ts`, and the seven commit messages.
- They state three things and nothing further: the defect exists (with no list, every origin was admitted for credentialed cross-origin requests, and `*` with credentials was accepted); where it lives (the CORS middleware `HonoServerPlugin.init()` mounts); and the governing text (`docs/HARDENING.md` § CORS).
- They give no request sequence against a shipped endpoint, no description of what a foreign page could obtain, and no unauthenticated-surface detail.
- The new pin file drives a probe route of its own through `app.request` and reads one header. It is the fix's evidence, as the claim comment foresaw, not a reproduction against a deployment.
- **The PR keeps to the ruling.** This record keeps to it as well.

**Check-runs on the head (latest run per name, 40 names).**
- 32 are `completed/success` and 5 are `completed/skipped` (opt-in and live-DB gates).
- **3 were still `in_progress` at render time: `Test Core (2/6)`, `Test Core (3/6)` and `Test Core (4/6)`. They are NOT MEASURED, never a pass.**
- `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check PR Size`, every `Lint ·` and `Type Check ·` job, `Build Core`, `Build Docs` and `Test Core (1/6, 5/6, 6/6)` concluded `success`.
- The judgments below are on the diff. The landing's own all-green check stands apart from this verdict and waits on those three shards.

**The accept-set changes the diff implies: the PR body's `## Contract` table, row by row, against the code.** "Admitted" means the request origin is echoed in `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. `init()` is the arrow property at `hono-plugin.ts:280`, and the CORS block (`:370-460`) sits inside it.

1. **No list, credentials on, not a development boot: every origin → no cross-origin caller. RIGHT.**
   - `configuredOrigin` stays `undefined`, because the `else { configuredOrigin = '*' }` arm is deleted.
   - The origin handler is `developmentBoot && isLocalhostOrigin(o) ? o : null`, and `developmentBoot = isDevelopmentBoot(undefined)` = `NODE_ENV === 'development'` (`core/src/stack-auth.ts:135`). So it answers `null` for every origin.
   - Pinned (describe 1).
2. **No list, credentials on, development boot: loopback only, with credentials. RIGHT.**
   - It is the same handler with `developmentBoot` true, and `credentials: true` still reaches `hono/cors`.
   - `isLocalhostOrigin` admits `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]`, over http or https, on any port: exactly the docs' list.
   - Pinned (describe 3).
3. **No list, `OS_CORS_CREDENTIALS=false`, either boot (rows 3 and 4): no cross-origin caller, or loopback only, without credentials. RIGHT.**
   - The default handler never reads `credentials`, so these rows differ from rows 1 and 2 only in the credentials header.
   - Not pinned in the credentials-off variant. The code path is the same expression.
4. **A list holding `*` (option or `OS_CORS_ORIGIN`, alone or among other entries), credentials on: `init()` throws. RIGHT.**
   - The check is `credentials && normalizeOriginPatterns(configuredOrigin).includes('*')`. `normalizeOriginPatterns` trims every entry and splits a comma string, so `['*']`, `' * '`, `'https://app.example.com,*'` and the option and env spellings all reach the throw.
   - The message names `OS_CORS_ORIGIN` and `OS_CORS_CREDENTIALS` and carries no tracker number.
   - Both kernels rethrow an `init()` throw unwrapped. `LiteKernel.bootstrap()` has no try around Phase 1, and `ObjectKernelBase.runPluginInit` rethrows after logging (`kernel-base.ts:204-206`). `ObjectKernel.bootstrap()` catches, rolls back nothing (nothing started yet) and does `throw error` (`kernel.ts:632-668`).
   - In `serve.ts` the construction sits inside a `try` that wraps only `kernel.use()`, which is registration only (`:3768-3778`). The throw surfaces at bootstrap and reaches the command's outer catch, which exits 1.
   - This is the same route as `@objectstack/plugin-dev`'s `assertNotProduction` (`dev-plugin.ts:127`, called from `init()` at `:500`), as claimed.
   - The "Before" column (booted and admitted every origin) is RIGHT for every spelling. The old `'*' && credentials` arm reflected the origin, and an array or list containing `*` went through `createOriginMatcher`, whose `matchOriginPattern(o, '*')` is true for all.
   - Pinned (describe 4, including the kernel-bootstrap case).

**The "Unchanged" list.**
- **A list without `*`, exact or patterns, admitted as before, with loopback alongside it: RIGHT.**
  - The old code reached `createOriginMatcher` on both arms (one wrapped in a lambda), and the new code calls it once.
  - `pattern-matcher.ts` is untouched, and its `matchOriginPattern` still returns true for any loopback origin ahead of the pattern.
  - An EMPTY list (`cors.origins: []`, or `OS_CORS_ORIGIN` of whitespace) makes the matcher admit nothing, loopback included. That is unchanged from before and narrower than the sentence reads; no accept set moves.
- **`*` with credentials off boots and admits any origin without credentials: RIGHT.** It is not refused, and `createOriginMatcher('*')` echoes the request origin as it did before. Pinned.
- **`cors: false`, `cors.enabled: false` and `OS_CORS_ENABLED=false` mount nothing: RIGHT.** That code is untouched.
- **Headers, methods and max-age unchanged, and preflights still answered: RIGHT.** The `cors()` options other than `origin` are untouched, and `hono/cors` answers OPTIONS itself whether or not it sets an allow-origin. Pin 1 reads the preflight's missing allow-origin.
- **Same-origin requests are outside CORS, and the Console is unaffected: RIGHT.** A browser applies the allow-origin check to cross-origin fetches only. A same-origin non-GET request does carry `Origin`, gets no allow-origin header under the new default, and is still readable. So nothing here needs the host's own origin, as the body says.
- **No export, option, type or spec key moves, and `HonoCorsOptions` gains TSDoc only: RIGHT.**
  - `adapter.ts` changes TSDoc only.
  - `hono-plugin.ts` drops its own import of `hasWildcardPattern`, but `index.ts:6` still has `export * from './pattern-matcher'`, and `@objectstack/hono` (`adapters/hono/src/index.ts:45,651`) still consumes it. `HonoPluginOptions.cors` keeps its type.
  - `isDevelopmentBoot` is a new value import from `@objectstack/core`, which is already a runtime dependency (`package.json` dependencies) and is already value-imported by `adapter.ts`. No new edge.
  - `Type Check · workspace` concluded success.

**Public-surface change outside the table.** The diff adds a new boot refusal (the thrown message) and changes a debug log line (`origin: admits`, which is a label, not the list). Both are RIGHT and documented. Nothing else on the published surface moves.

**One precision note on the development-boot claim.** Its direction is narrow, so it is not an accept-set defect.
- The transport reads development-ness as `NODE_ENV === 'development'` only (`isDevelopmentBoot(undefined)`).
- `serve` reads `isDevelopmentBoot(flags.dev)` for itself, and sets `NODE_ENV=development` under `--dev` **only when `NODE_ENV` is unset** (`serve.ts:2176-2177`). `os dev` leaves it to serve (`dev.ts:569-576`).
- The prose faces say `NODE_ENV=development`, "which `os dev` and `os serve --dev` set". That is true on the documented path. On a boot that exports another `NODE_ENV` and passes `--dev`, serve's own development conveniences apply, but the CORS default admits no loopback origin.
- The rule itself ("`NODE_ENV` exactly `development`") is stated exactly in every face, so the statement of shipped behaviour holds; the parenthetical is one edge short.
- Non-blocking. The dispatching seat may name it in ACCEPT.

**Prose faces, each against the shipped behaviour.**
- **`environment-variables.mdx`: TRUE.** Its CORS rows say: the default is `—`; unset means no cross-origin caller, with loopback excepted on a development boot; `*` is refused unless credentials are off; and `OS_CORS_CREDENTIALS` must be `false` for `*`. Its port note says `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` is auth CSRF (`serve.ts:4182`).
- **`self-hosting.mdx`: TRUE.** No entry is needed same-origin; a foreign front-end needs `OS_CORS_ORIGIN`; and never `*` while credentials are on.
- **`production-readiness.mdx`: TRUE.** The checklist item matches the code.
- **`README.md`: TRUE.** It states the default, the refusal at init, the `OS_CORS_*` spellings, and that legacy `CORS_*` names are still read (`readEnvWithDeprecation`, silent).
- **`docs/HARDENING.md` § CORS: TRUE.**
  - The three-row table is TRUE, and "loopback admitted alongside any list" is TRUE for a non-empty list.
  - The `createHonoApp` example is correctly worded as "name the origins there as well".
  - The refusal is scoped to `HonoServerPlugin`. The page does not claim the adapter refuses, which it does not (see ③).
- **The changeset's Before / Now / Unchanged and "What an operator does": TRUE**, with the same `--dev` parenthetical as above.

**Consumer tests in the diff.** All three changes are RIGHT and minimal.
- `http-metrics-inbound-coverage.hono.integration.test.ts` names the origin its preflight carries (`https://app.test`) instead of `'*'` with credentials, which the boot now refuses. The pin's premise still holds: the transport's CORS built-in answers the preflight before the metrics seam.
- The two http-conformance door-parity pins now boot both doors with `cors: false`, as the suite's other parity pins do. CORS headers were never what they compare.

### ② Semver level

- **The changeset matches what the diff publishes.** `.changeset/24738-cors-default-no-cross-origin-caller.md` carries `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server: minor`, a **BREAKING** banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, and the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The PR body's second line carries the same `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. Only `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server` moves published source. The other six code paths are tests (`packages/qa/http-conformance` and a `packages/runtime` test file), which publish nothing. One changeset is right, and `skip-changeset` would be wrong.
- **Level: RIGHT.**
  - An accept-set narrowing of a shipped default is breaking.
  - `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` is still armed: `.changeset/pre.json` is `mode: exit` with tag `next`, the packages are at `18.0.0-next.5`, and the guard's end condition (its own retirement at GA) has not happened. So `major` is refused, and the launch-window form is `minor` plus a BREAKING banner plus an ADR-0087 disposition.
  - That is the form of every narrowing changeset on `main`: `24341-extend-default-row-scope-refused.md` and 18 siblings, all `minor`. `patch` would understate it, since the `fix(` type never lowers the level the act requires.
  - `Check Changeset` concluded success on the head.
- **ADR-0087 disposition: RIGHT.** No authorable key, spelling, export, type or stored shape moves, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite. The body's "What an operator does" is a deployment-variable step, not a consumer-code migration prescription, so the gate's statement-against-statement refusal does not fire. The ruling that 18.0.0 ships this (card comments `6284880389`, `6285370999`) is consistent with a `minor` under the window.
- **`Clause-②` line: `no (narrowing)` is RIGHT.** No new key lands on any published payload, and one accept set narrows. It is what owes this `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record on the narrowing face.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev's flags (report `6285567675`, deviations and acceptance notes) and the one `open_questions` entry:

1. **Three files outside the claim's file surface** (the runtime metrics pin and two http-conformance parity pins). Answered: they are the in-repo consumers the narrowing broke, read above, and each change minimally names its configuration. Accepted.
2. **Attribution trailer form, gate-runner timing, two merges of `main`.** Not contract matters. This record reads the merge-base diff, and `main` has since moved one commit on disjoint paths. No action.
3. **Sibling default in `@objectstack/hono`'s `createHonoApp`** (`packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts:606-680`, read). It keeps the old default: no list resolves to `*`, and `*` with credentials reflects the request origin. It is outside this card's file surface and the claim's hold-offs, and `HARDENING.md` now tells a host composing it to name its origins. **Escalated: the seat files it as a `security` card in the same family (the dev's dedupe words), under the same disclosure ruling. It does not block this PR**: the card's reader is the plugin owner, and the adapter is a separate published package with its own option shape.
4. **Loopback admitted alongside any configured list, in every mode** (`matchOriginPattern`, shared with cloud's preflight short-circuit). Answered: the card scopes "localhost in dev only" to the default, the matcher is untouched, and `HARDENING.md` states the behaviour. Whether that convenience should also become development-only is the maintainer's call. It is a note, not a card from this record.
5. **`cli.mdx:523` still calls `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` "(CORS)".** It is held off for PR #24681. Answered: whichever lands second corrects the line.
6. **`CorsConfigSchema` in spec (`origins` default `'*'`, `credentials` default `false`).** The transport does not read it, and it is the spec lane's, held off. Answered: the future `server.cors` admission should carry this PR's default. Noted for that card.
7. **A degenerate pattern such as `https://*` is not refused.** Answered: it is operator-configured and outside the card's default, and it is reported in the PR. No action here.
8. **`http-protocol.mdx` "CORS Headers" example.** Answered: it shows an admitted, configured origin. One clarifying line is a docs follow-up; the page is not false today.
9. **Cloud composition NOT MEASURED.** Answered as a landing-adjacent flag. `createOriginMatcher` is unchanged, so cloud's preflight short-circuit is unaffected. Whether any cloud deployment serves a cross-origin front-end with no `OS_CORS_ORIGIN` cannot be measured from this repo. The changeset states the operator step, and the seat should name it to the maintainer when cloud takes `18.0.0`.
10. **`--dev` with an exported `NODE_ENV`** (this record's own finding, ① above). It fails narrow, and at most it needs a one-word docs precision.

**Open question: should `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` also feed CORS?** It is the maintainer's to answer. **The shipped answer (A: keep the lists separate) is safe to land pending that ruling.**
- A is the narrowest of the three and admits nothing the card did not ask to admit.
- B (add the explicit `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` entries) is a pure widening on top of A. It can be adopted later as a `Clause-②: yes`-shaped follow-up without a second breaking change.
- C (serve's full resolution, with the preview and root-domain wildcards) would import auth's CSRF wildcards into credentialed CORS. It is the widest of the three, and the dev's own analysis names it the worst.
- Shipping B or C first and narrowing later would be the unsafe order.
- The one cost of A: a cross-origin front-end that set only `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` loses CORS admission on upgrade, at boot and in the browser. That cost is stated in the changeset, `HARDENING.md` and `self-hosting.mdx`.
- **The landing must not wait.** The ruling is owed on the card before any B or C widening is dispatched.

**Landing.** The 18.0.0 ruling is recorded (`6284880389`, `6285370999`), and this record is the narrowing face's review of record. Still owed before the queue: every check green (three `Test Core` shards were in progress at render), and the lane's own main-red hold (#24780), as the card states.
